newsitem.title: GERMANY: German M3 growth steady in October, Ifo index jumps.
newsitem.headline: German M3 growth steady in October, Ifo index jumps.

text.p: Germany's Bundesbank said on Wednesday that M3 money supply growth expanded at a headline annualised rate of 8.4 percent in October, unchanged from the September growth rate.
Separately, the respected German Ifo economics institute said its October survey showed a sharp jump in the business climate index last month to 97.4 percent from 95.7.

German bonds slipped to their day's low on the Ifo figure, which indicated that the German economy was recovering more strongly than many had believed. The December bund future fell 0.15 point to 101.03.
The market had already been unsettled by the M3 data, which also showed stronger than expected growth.
In its statement, the Bundesbank warned that growth in its main economic indicator -- which has consistently grown beyond target this year -- had gained pace on average in the month.
Lending, and domestic public lending in particular, had a particularly expansive effect, it said.
Strong growth in sight deposits was apparently linked to money being parked in such accounts ahead of the huge issue of 713 million Deutsche Telekom AG shares this week, it said.
